next: Dictations made with SonoJot Parakeet no longer capitalise a word in the middle of a sentence after a pause.
Highlighted choices, such as the selected fix in the doubtful-words card, now look like raised paper instead of plain white, and focus rings go round the whole control.

Meetings on speakers: Remove speaker echo (Sources and speakers) removes the other people's words that your microphone picked up, so they no longer appear twice as yours. It is on automatically with SonoJot Parakeet and off with Qwen until you turn it on; turn it off and transcribe again to get the unfiltered text.
Meetings and imported recordings transcribed with Parakeet on an NVIDIA graphics card no longer stop partway through long stretches of speech.
A meeting's Clean copy no longer capitalises a word in the middle of a sentence after a pause, as dictation already did not.

After a paste, SonoJot marks the few words it doubts right in the app you pasted into: hover to hear them, pick a fix, keep them, or hold the dictation key and say the word. Settings: Dictation, Doubtful words.
A test copy of SonoJot started with its own data folder no longer adds itself to coding tools.
Set up sync and Add this computer now open SonoJot email-code pages, with a clear recovery-code step for your first computer.
Removing a lost device changes the encryption key; your other trusted computers update automatically on their next sync, and SonoJot asks you to save the new recovery code.

Cleanup puts back the space before words like 'cause, 'til and 'em when the speech model joins them to the previous sentence, and Clean keeps leading apostrophes, opening quotes and brackets in place.
Switching update channels offers a clear download and restart action, or explains when no build is available for your computer.
Nightly releases now include signed and notarized builds for Apple Silicon Macs when the Mac build succeeds.
Builds without a configured staging server keep vocabulary sync disabled and explain why.
Mac sync sign-in explains keychain errors; the separate Sync Test app can save its test credentials without unlocking the login keychain.
Encrypted vocabulary sync is available in nightly and other prerelease builds; stable builds keep sync disabled.
Sync Test can sign into isolated staging test accounts and pause its connection from the command line.
The Updates screen and the update prompt are tidier: buttons line up, and a long download no longer pushes the side bar out of place.
After an update, SonoJot no longer says it closed unexpectedly. It shows what's new instead.
See changes shows what an update brings before you install it, and What's new in Settings > Updates shows the notes for your version.
Meetings and imported recordings miss fewer words, including quiet speech such as a stretch where you sit back from the microphone.

New speech model: SonoJot Parakeet, our own tuned version of Parakeet. It makes about a fifth fewer errors on dictation than Parakeet in our tests, at the same size and speed. It replaces Parakeet in the speech list. If you use Parakeet now, nothing changes until you choose the new one.

New English setups now start on SonoJot Parakeet for dictation and meetings on every computer, including NVIDIA PCs and Macs. It ties Qwen3-ASR on meetings in our tests and is faster and smaller. Qwen3-ASR stays one tap away in Speech as the multilingual choice, other languages keep Qwen, and your saved choices do not change.
On a Mac, the Speech screen now shows word errors measured in the Mac app for SonoJot Parakeet and Qwen3-ASR, and the chart marks SonoJot Parakeet as recommended.

The Speech page is calmer: each model is one simple card with a short line, and the details sit behind a small i button. Compare models opens one chart of every model this computer can run, for everyday speech, accented English or talks, with a table of the same numbers. In Cleanup, Punctuation and the optional Proofreader now have their own rows, and the details for other settings moved behind i buttons.

It replaces Parakeet in the speech list and is the Balanced choice for new English setups on computers without an NVIDIA graphics card or Apple Silicon. If you use Parakeet now, nothing changes until you choose the new one.
A time such as "2:30 PM on Friday" no longer gets a stray period that starts a new sentence, and abbreviations such as "e.g." and "etc." keep their periods.
Times after words like "until" are written as times, for example "until 10:50".
Cleanup of long dictations is faster: it uses more of the processor when the computer is idle and less when it is busy.
The first nightly build after 0.28.9. It has the same features as 0.28.9.

A new look. SonoJot now has four places down the left side: Dictation, Meetings, Words and Settings. Each list has a status band on top that shows what is ready and opens the right setting when something needs attention.
Speech models are compared on one chart of measured speed and memory, with the recommended choices shown first.
Choose your update channel in Settings > Updates: Stable, or Nightly for early test builds. Switch back to Stable at any time.
Meetings: rename a speaker or move a single passage to another speaker, search titles, notes and transcripts, and pick a notes style that is written automatically after each transcription.
Words: a word on its own is now a hint that helps SonoJot spell it without forcing a replacement. "Heard as > written" rules still replace exactly.
Dictation: export any dictation as Markdown, and choose to keep nothing, text, or text and audio. Audio stays on your computer for 30 days.
Fixes: pasted API keys stay hidden, shortcuts and notes instructions are checked before saving, and an update now finishes even when the command-line tool is running.

New, experimental: proofread your dictations with an online model. Turn on "Proofread with an online model" in Dictation to fix misheard words, typos and false starts while keeping your wording. It uses your own OpenRouter account and is off unless you turn it on.
Shape by type is easier to find: it now has its own row in Dictation. A new option, "Use the app I'm in", lays out text to suit where you are typing.
Saved dictations now note which app they were meant for, on your computer only. The privacy notice and terms describe both changes.
